takeaway: Weak dorsiflexion, weak toe extension and numb first web space point to the anterior compartment (deep peroneal nerve); treat with fasciotomy.

question.text: A 21-year-old man has compartment syndrome with weak ankle dorsiflexion, weak toe extension and numbness of the first dorsal web space. Which compartment had raised pressure?

lines.text: In compartment syndrome, pressure inside a fascial compartment rises and chokes its blood flow.
Here the anterior compartment is swollen, and the gauge is deep in the red.
The deep peroneal nerve supplies this compartment, and it is squeezed.
So dorsiflexion of the ankle is weak,
and toe extension is weak too.
The first dorsal web space is the nerve's own sensory area, and it goes numb.
A fasciotomy opens the room. The raised pressure was in the anterior compartment.
lines.say: (sigh) A fasciotomy opens the room. The raised pressure was in the anterior compartment.
